title: Libyan-Style Fish in Spicy Tomato and Pepper Sauce
summary: Thick white fish fillets gently simmered in a fragrant, spicy sauce of tomato, red pepper, garlic and warm spices, finished with lemon and fresh herbs. Serve from the pan with crusty bread for mopping.
equipment: large deep frying pan or sauté pan (30 cm) with lid

ingredients.item: skinless thick white fish fillets, such as cod or haddock (about 150 g each)
fine sea salt or table salt
green chilli, seeded and finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Salt the fish
steps.text: Sprinkle the salt over the fillets and leave them on a plate while you make the sauce. Salting ahead gives the seasoning time to penetrate and firms the surface slightly, so the fish holds together better as it simmers.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Heat the olive oil in the pan over medium heat and add the onion, red pepper and chilli. Cook for 6-8 minutes until soft and sweet. Softening them fully at this stage gives the sauce a smooth, mellow base.

steps.title: Toast the spices
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, tomato purée, paprika, cumin, ground coriander, cayenne and pepper, and cook for 1-2 minutes. The purée should darken to brick red and smell toasty. Frying the purée and spices in oil before any water goes in deepens and rounds out their flavour.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Pour in the water, add the salt and scrape up any bits stuck to the pan. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 15 minutes until thickened. This gives the flavours time to meld before the fish goes in.

steps.title: Poach the fish
steps.text: Nestle the fillets into the sauce, spoon some over the tops and scatter the cherry tomatoes around. Cover and simmer very gently for 8-10 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes when prodded with a knife and reads at least 63°C in the thickest part. Low heat keeps the flesh moist and in whole pieces.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Drizzle over the lemon juice and scatter with the herbs. Serve straight from the pan with the bread to soak up the sauce.

tips: A common mistake is adding the water before the purée has darkened, which leaves the sauce tasting raw; give the spices their full 1-2 minutes.
Choose thick fillets, as thin pieces overcook and break apart in the sauce.
Adjust the cayenne to suit your taste; the sauce is meant to be lively but should not overwhelm the fish.
The sauce can be made up to the end of simmering a day ahead, then reheated before adding the fish.
storage: Cool within 2 hours, refrigerate and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan until piping hot (74°C).
